title: Much or little (Berakhot 17a)
hook: the sages of Yavneh: I work in town, he works in the field; much or little, what matters is the heart
tomorrow: no food, no rivals, no deadlines. so what is the world to come?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rava: dust while alive, unfinished and still asking. Today, two workers and two very different days.

On every team there's a ranking nobody says out loud. Cast and crew. The surgeon and the night cleaner. The one with the title and the one who stays late to lock up. So, the scholar or the farmer: who did more today? The sages of Yavneh had a favorite saying about exactly this, and it starts with both of them waking up early.
screen: `THE RANKING NOBODY SAYS.` → `SCHOLAR OR FARMER?` → `BOTH UP EARLY.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in plain words. I am a creature, and my fellow is a creature. My work is in the town, and his work is in the field. I rise early to my work, and he rises early to his. Just as he doesn't claim my work, I don't claim his. And in case you say, I do much and he does little: we've learned, one does much and one does little, as long as each directs the heart to heaven. That's the first voice, and its best case is strong. If the heart is what counts, the farmer and the scholar stand level, and so does the kid running the lights with the kid in the spotlight. Now a second voice, from Pirkei Avot. Ben Hei Hei says: according to the effort is the reward. Its best case is strong too. Effort is real. If more and less are treated as the same, someone coasts, and the person who carried the heavy end of the couch gets erased. Notice what the two don't fight about. Neither one says the study hall outranks the field. Neither says a job makes a person bigger. Here's the part to tell a friend tonight: the people saying "he's a creature like me" were the scholars, and the one they named as their equal was the man out in the field. The tradition keeps both voices on its shelf, the heart and the effort, and lets them check each other.

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person whose work looks nothing like yours: a driver, a cook, the person who cleans the building, a teammate in a different role. Draft a short thank-you text naming one thing their work makes possible for you. Send it whenever it feels right.

segments.voice: Much or little. The sages of Yavneh: my work in town, his in the field, and what matters is that each directs the heart to heaven.
Your line: much or little, the heart. The field and the study hall, side by side. Fourteen of fifty.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching holds study and honest work together, and the line 'one does much and one does little, as long as the heart is directed to heaven' is often quoted to honor every kind of effort.

fork.setup: your cousin loves the Yavneh saying and says effort doesn't matter, only the heart. what's the best case for the other side, from inside the tradition?
options: Avot: according to the effort is the reward, so the heavy lifting isn't erased.

fork.reveal: Ben Hei Hei in Pirkei Avot: according to the effort is the reward. the tradition keeps that beside the Yavneh saying, so heart and effort check each other.

original.note: Hebrew: one who does much and one who does little. the saying goes on: as long as the heart is directed to heaven.

chat.meaning: The Yavneh sages held town and field level: different work, both up early, and what counts is the heart directed to heaven.

Yavneh.meaning: a town where sages gathered and taught
